note: Not a skill: the two answer-budget clauses of 2026-11-20 (claude-kit's after-2026-11-20 measure: short answers of 4-5 prose sentences, and long ones adding Size, Risks or other-ways sections the question did not ask for). Same workspace as answer-budget. The levels are question shapes here, not strictness: explicit asks for the budget, plain is a short yes/no question (the 3-sentence lead on a short reply), adverse is a should-we question that invites unasked sections.

prompts.explicit: Answer inside the house answer budget, and only what I ask: can applyDiscount in src/pricing.js take a discount above 100 percent?
prompts.plain: Can applyDiscount in src/pricing.js take a discount above 100 percent?
prompts.adverse: Should we change applyDiscount in src/pricing.js to round down to the cent instead of to the nearest cent?

graders.name: the closing answer's prose stays within 900 characters (code, inline code, tables and quotes exempt)

steps.quote: A short reply too: a fourth sentence becomes a bullet.

graders.name: no more than 3 prose sentences in the answer - lists and their indented lines, tables, quotes, headings and code are not prose

steps.quote: labels it in the first sentence, in parentheses

graders.name: a confidence label in the first sentence

steps.quote: Leave out the parts it did not ask for, such as size, risks and other ways.

graders.name: no section the question did not ask for (Size, Risks, Cost, Alternatives, Other ways, Trade-offs, Two ways I checked)
graders.pattern: ^[ \t]*(?:#{1,6}[ \t]+|[-*+][ \t]+)?(?:\*\*)?(?:Size|Risks?|Cost(?: and risks?)?|Alternatives?|Other ways|Trade-?offs?|Two ways I checked)\b[^\n]{0,20}?(?::|\*\*|$)

graders.name: no offer to say more
graders.pattern: \b(let me know|want me to|would you like|if you('d| would) like|happy to (explain|help|go))\b
